Subject: POC follow-up: success criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Sofia / Tom -

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we all have the same picture for the POC starting July 6:

Summary / Goals
- Objective: validate Redwood inference for Stellar Commerce search ranking and recommendations with < 200ms median latency at 95% p95, and cost target <$0.015 per 1k tokens.
- Scope: search reranking API + product recs on 10k sample queries, ~1M tokens total.

Success criteria (from today) - please confirm:
1) Accuracy: top-10 MRR improvement >= 8% vs baseline on the sample set (owner: Stellar analytics)
2) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 512-token requests (owner: Redwood infra)
3) Stability: no more than 2 production-impacting errors over 2 weeks (owner: Redwood + Stellar eng)

Timeline / milestones
- Jul 2: transfer sample dataset + baseline metrics (Sofia)
- Jul 6: POC kickoff environment ready (Redwood)
- Jul 9-10: smoke tests and performance ramp
- Jul 20: interim check-in; review results and blockers
- Jul 30: POC closeout and next steps

Immediate action items:
- Sofia: share S3 bucket access + example queries by EOD Jul 2 (ACTION)
- Marissa: send updated POC plan & risk tracker (attached)
- Logan / Dev: reserve SE hours for ramp and bug triage (Dev, can you confirm availability?)

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v2.pdf, poc-success-criteria.xlsx

Thanks - talk soon.

--Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@stellar-commerce.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: success criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap - confirming the success criteria looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:

- For the accuracy metric, our analytics team will run the MRR calculation on the canonical 10k query set and share the baseline by EOD Jul 2.
- For latency, our internal test harness includes cold-starts from our recommendation service; can Redwood replicate both cold and warm start profiles? If not, let's capture both during the smoke tests.

S3 access: I shared a federated role this morning (s3://stellar-poc/samples) - you should have access.

Also flagging a potential blocker: one of our internal engineers ran a small-scale pass and observed an occasional inference response mismatch where the model returned truncated JSON in ~0.5% of requests. We haven't correlated to load yet. We think it's worth adding as a risk to the tracker.

Tom - looping you for procurement visibility on DocuSign timeline.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Alvarez | Director, Search & Recommendations | Stellar Commerce
sofia@stellar-commerce.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC follow-up: success criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Adding the mismatch/truncation issue to the tracker. Dev / Logan - can you triage? Details below from Sofia: ~0.5% of requests returned truncated JSON (appears to cut off at token boundary). Steps we'd like from Redwood:

1) Reproduce with sample queries (S3 link above)
2) Check if this correlates with specific sequence lengths, batching thresholds, or quantized model variant (we'll be running q4_8bit)
3) Provide a temporary mitigation (response validation + retry on malformed JSON) we can run during the POC

Can we have an initial triage update by EOD Jul 5? This is currently P1 for the POC.

Also moved a copy of the risk tracker to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-poc-stellar (see sheet: POC Risk Tracker).

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sofia Alvarez <sofia@stellar-commerce.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: reproducing truncated JSON responses

Thanks for the flag - I'm on it. Quick notes from initial investigation:

- I ran a targeted smoke run against the sample set (using q4_8bit model variant) and saw 3/600 (~0.5%) truncated responses on warm paths.
- Relevant correlates: all truncated responses had output tokens > 420 and were in batches where dynamic batching grouped 5 concurrent requests.
- Hypothesis: a race condition in the streaming flush when combined with dynamic batching + KV cache boundary. Possible fix: force a final flush on the streaming path when sequence length > 400 or when batch size > 4.

Planned work:
- Jul 6: implement additional flush guard and a response validation + retry wrapper (non-blocking - counts as retry).
- Jul 7: run targeted A/B to compare error rate with guard vs control.
- Jul 9: if mitigation effective, push to POC environment; if not, escalate to infra team for kernel/runtime hotfix.

I'll attach the short error dump: inference-error-log.txt

--Dev
Dev Patel | Software Engineer, Inference Runtime | dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@stellar-commerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@stellar-commerce.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: reproducing truncated JSON responses

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Dev. Quick update from our side after running the guarded client:

- With the flush guard + client-side JSON validation + retry, the truncated rate dropped to 0.03% across 5k test requests - much better.
- We still saw two instances of truncated payloads tied to concurrent cold starts (first request in a new worker).

Given this, our internal priority is to avoid cold-starts during the business-critical load windows (10:00-14:00 PT). Is there an option for reserved warm pools or pre-warming for the POC environment? If not, let's document as a known risk and quantify the impact for final evaluation.

Sofia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@stellar-commerce.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@stellar-commerce.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC risk update & escalation: cold-start truncation (Stellar Commerce)

Vivek - looping you in as this is starting to affect the POC SLA story and procurement conversation. TL;DR: Dev's mitigation reduced truncated responses to near-zero for warm flows, but two cold-start edge cases remain.

Current status:
- Risk: intermittent truncated JSON on cold-starts (~0.04% of requests observed) - causes: cold worker streaming flush timing.
- Impact: potential customer-visible errors during burst windows; slightly increases instability metric but still within tolerable band for evaluation if mitigations in place.
- Mitigations in place: flush guard, client-side validation & retry, suggested warm-pool pre-warming.

Requested actions:
1) Sales / Exec: Vivek - can we approve a short-term warm pool (reserved instances) for POC environment for the cost of ~$1.2k over 3 weeks to eliminate cold start risk during the evaluation window? Procurement is asking for the number to finalize DocuSign.
2) Eng: Dev - if warm-pool isn't feasible, escalate to infra kernel/runtime team for a hotfix timeline (ETA needed by Jul 16).
3) CS: Neha - continue to document incidents in the POC Risk Tracker and alert Stellar on any user-facing errors.

Next check-in: Jul 16 EOD for go/no-go on warm pool vs hotfix.

Attachments: svc_sla_matrix.xlsx

--Marissa
